sources: 1901: sponge divers recover finds from the Antikythera shipwreck (Roman era, c. 60s BC); May 1902: a gear wheel is noticed in a corroded fragment at the National Archaeological Museum, Athens (Spyridon and Valerios Stais). Linda Hall Library, 'Scientist of the Day' (2024); Wikipedia 'Antikythera mechanism'.

More than 30 hand-cut bronze gears; nothing comparable built for another thousand years; dated 150–100 BC; tracked sun and moon, predicted eclipses; X-ray tomography 2005–06. Freeth et al. (2006), 'Decoding the ancient Greek astronomical calculator known as the Antikythera Mechanism', Nature 444, 587–591; Live Science (2006); NYT (30 Nov 2006).
'Oldest known analog computer': IEEE REACH; History.com (2025). 'Some said: aliens' = popular ancient-astronaut claim, no evidence.
